title: Students protest online-only teaching and education costs outside the Ministry of Education
organizer: Students; organizational relationship among the Ministry group and other student groups is not established.
participants_original: Citizens.al describes “dozens” on 2 November; the 3 November report says attendance was smaller.
threshold_50_evidence: Not established. “Dozens” is imprecise and does not prove 50 or more; no exact count is reported.

start_date.summary: Contemporary reports date the Ministry protest to 2 November.

location.summary: Reports place students at or outside the Ministry of Education in Tirana.

demands.summary: Reported requests concern ending online-only learning/returning to in-person teaching and lower tuition or related study costs.

participants_original.summary: Citizens.al and Anadolu use “dozens”; the day-two report says turnout was smaller than the previous day.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No exact count; qualitative “dozens” does not establish 50+.

state_response.crowd_dispersal.summary: Police called for dispersal/asked the demonstrators to stop; S001 says police then allowed the demonstration to continue.

state_response.accommodation.summary: The prime minister publicly said dormitory payments would be refunded, but the report does not establish a causal link to the protest or implementation; left unknown.

notes: S019 identifies 3 November as the second day and smaller than 2 November. A 4 November search-result title calls it a third day, but its URL returned 404 and is not body evidence; end date remains unknown. Do not combine the separate Movement for the University march to the Prime Minister’s Office (E002). KOHA’s /BW marker indicates likely Balkanweb material, so it is not treated as independent confirmation. No daily attendance count is available.
open_questions: Did any day of this gathering reach 50 participants?
When did the Ministry gathering end?
Were dormitory refunds a response to the protest and were they implemented?
Are any reports reprints from the same original outlet?

title: Movement for the University students march to the Prime Minister’s Office over tuition and student support
organizer: Movement for the University (reported by Citizens.al); relation to the Ministry of Education gathering is unclear.
threshold_50_evidence: Unknown. Citizens.al describes a separate march and press conference but gives no participant count.

start_date.summary: Citizens.al reports this separate group action on 2 November.

location.summary: The report places the Movement for the University group at the Prime Minister’s Office.

organizer.summary: Citizens.al attributes the march and press conference to Movement for the University.

demands.summary: The report describes demands about half tuition and a social package/living support.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No attendance figure or qualitative 50+ estimate appears.

notes: Keep separate from E001 because the source distinguishes the groups, locations and requests. No evidence supports aggregating their numbers.
open_questions: Was this a distinct event or part of the larger student campaign?
Any state response or event end date?

title: Civil-society and labor-rights activity calling for restoration of assembly and protest rights
organizer: Civic Center, Centre for Labour Rights and Olof Palme Center (as reported by the Agency for the Support of Civil Society).
threshold_50_evidence: Not established. The official newsletter gives no headcount and does not specify whether the activity was a public demonstration.

start_date.summary: Official newsletter dates the activity to 5 November in Tirana.

location.summary: The newsletter gives Tirana but not a venue.

organizer.summary: The newsletter names Civic Center, Centre for Labour Rights and Olof Palme Center as organizers.

demands.summary: Participants sought restoration of assembly/protest rights and sent an open letter to national institutions.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No headcount or clear public-gathering form is given; threshold and inclusion remain uncertain.

notes: The source calls this an “activity”; it may be an advocacy meeting rather than an eligible public gathering. Keep as a candidate because its form, public character and attendance are unspecified.
open_questions: Was this a public gathering of at least 50 people?
What was the venue and format?

title: Bulqiza miners and residents collect signatures for a petition on miners’ status
organizer: United Union of Miners of Bulqiza
participants_original: “Dozens” of miners are reported as undertaking the initiative; the article also says miners and citizens gathered to sign.
threshold_50_evidence: Uncertain. “Dozens” can refer to under or over 50, and no precise count is reported; the three-day signature collection may not have had a constant daily turnout.

start_date.summary: The Citizens.al article says the petition gathering lasted three days; the embedded union post dates the start to 23 November.

end_date.summary: The article says signature collection had gathered people for three days by its 26 November publication; the embedded post dates the start to 23 November, suggesting 23–25 November.

location.summary: The article places signature collection in Bulqiza town square.

organizer.summary: The United Union of Miners of Bulqiza is identified with the initiative.

demands.summary: The petition asks Parliament and government to approve a legal status for miners, including improved financial, retirement, insurance and health provisions.

participants_original.summary: The report says “dozens” of miners undertook the initiative and describes miners and citizens gathering to sign over three days; exact counts are absent.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: “Dozens” is too imprecise to verify 50+; no numeric count is reported.

notes: The petition is directed to Parliament and government and was conducted by signature collection in a town square. Do not code the 3,200 miners mentioned in the article as participants; it describes the local workforce, not petition attendance. Exact daily turnout and whether the three-day period maps precisely to 23–25 November remain unverified.
open_questions: Did at least 50 people gather on any day?
How many signatures or people attended per day?
Does this signature-collection activity satisfy the project’s public-gathering definition?
